title: Multinegativity and single-letter formulas for asymptotic entanglement
authors: Raphael Brinster, Tulja Varun Kondra, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Nikolai Wyderka
abstract: The study of entanglement inevitably leads to the concept of regularization, where measures are evaluated on infinitely many copies of a state. Single-letter formulas try to make these asymptotic entanglement quantities accessible through a calculation on one copy of a state, but are rarely available. We introduce a decreasing hierarchy of computable upper bounds on the asymptotic relative entropy of entanglement with respect to positive-partial-transpose (PPT) states. The regularization of every fixed hierarchy level equals this asymptotic quantity. Additivity at any level therefore yields a single-letter formula, even when the usual one-copy relative entropy is nonadditive. We establish such additivity at the first nontrivial level for two broad multiparameter families, both containing all Werner states. The upper-bound construction also extends to sandwiched Renyi divergences. The hierarchy motivates $k$-multinegative states, a generalization of binegative states and the associated $k$-multinegativity, which gives explicit upper bounds on both the asymptotic relative entropy and exact PPT entanglement cost. We construct states which are $k$-multinegative at arbitrarily large depths $k$ that separate consecutive levels of the previously introduced entanglement-cost hierarchy, disproving its conjectured finite collapse. These results provide state-dependent single-letter formulas while identifying a limitation of universal finite-level characterizations.
summary: This paper develops a structured hierarchy of computable upper bounds for asymptotic entanglement measures, such as the relative entropy of entanglement with respect to PPT states. By showing that the regularization of these bounds yields the true asymptotic value, the authors provide state-dependent single-letter formulas. Crucially, they also construct counterexamples demonstrating that these entanglement cost hierarchies do not collapse at any finite level.
main_problem: The central problem is finding single-letter formulas for complex, asymptotic entanglement quantities, such as the asymptotic relative entropy of entanglement with respect to PPT states ($E_\infty^R$).
main_result: The authors introduce a computable, decreasing hierarchy of upper bounds ($	ilde{E}_{1N,k}$) that regularizes to the true asymptotic entanglement measure, while also constructing states that disprove the conjecture of a finite collapse for entanglement cost hierarchies.
method: The work employs the construction of a hierarchy of constrained sets ($	ext{PPT}_k$, $	ext{]PPT}_k$) and utilizes convex optimization (semidefinite programming) to derive single-letter upper bounds on entanglement measures.

paper_structure: The paper first introduces the hierarchy of upper bounds using single-letter formulas, then establishes additivity for specific state families, and finally motivates $k$-multinegativity, culminating in the construction of counterexamples that show the hierarchy does not collapse at finite levels.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, computable tools (single-letter formulas) to approximate notoriously difficult-to-calculate asymptotic entanglement measures, which is fundamental to understanding quantum resource theories.
